worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{-1}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{-1}^{-6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-9\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{-1}(3f(x)+8)\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{-6}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,8{\int }_{-6}^{-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(-9)\,+\,8\cdot x\,{|}_{-6}^{-1} \\  & =-27\,+\,8((-1)-(-6)) \\  & =-27\,+\,40 \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$
